$comment: The recorded state of the `endora new instance` acceptance criterion
(`specs/110-instance-repository/` FR-011, contracts/instance-repository.md §6, T140).
`acceptance:instance:ci` compares a run to this file and fails on drift in EITHER
direction: a newly-red assertion fails, and so does a newly-green one nobody recorded.
An unrecorded pass is a criterion whose meaning moved without anybody reading it.
IT LANDED WITH TWO REDS AND EIGHT UNMEASURED, AND THAT WAS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A
SHORTFALL OF THE INSTRUMENT. Before this file existed nothing had ever run a scaffolded
instance: `packages/cli/test/new-instance.test.ts` asserts the plan, and the merge
request before it (!1580) took the created backend to `tsc` exit 0 and said in as
many words that a type-check was the whole of the evidence. The first run of this
criterion found that the tree compiles, installs, and then does nothing at all.
T141 REPAIRED FOUR OF THE FIVE DEFECTS THAT RUN FOUND, AND THE FIFTH IS NOW DISCHARGED
TOO. The fifth was a schema decision rather than a wiring one — the platform's own
migration corpus was not self-contained, so an instance omitting a module could not
migrate at all — and `specs/120-migration-closure-bridge-ownership/` answered it across
five merge requests. A3 passes: 118 migrations, exit 0, and A4 with it — the instance boots,
answers 200 and accounts for every module it enumerates. The one red is A8's, and it is the
finding of T141/T142 rather than a shortfall: see that entry.
EVERY NON-PASS ENTRY BELOW NAMES THE CONTRACT OR TASK IT WAITS ON, AND THAT RULE IS
ENFORCED RATHER THAN INTENDED. `expectationRefusals` in
`../scripts/acceptance/instance-assertions.ts` refuses this file — exit 2, not a drift —
when a non-`pass` entry carries no reason, or a reason that names neither a task (T###)
nor a contract, or one of the four spellings of the word the row calls out:
`unimplemented`, `not implemented`, `TODO`, `not started`.
THE `registry` MODE IS `unrun` AND NOT AN EMPTY `recorded`. A supply route nobody has
measured owes no assertion states, and writing a prediction of them is the thing this
file exists to refuse. The first run with ENDORA_NPM_REGISTRY set drifts — naming every
assertion it measured — which is what makes that record arrive from a measurement.
THERE ARE FIFTEEN ASSERTIONS AND THE NUMBERING IS SETTLED. `instance-repository.md`
R6.3 numbers A1…A13, its A13 being FR-023/SC-011's built-admin-stylesheet assertion;
`instance-tree.md` §6 opens by declaring the criterion to be §6's UNCHANGED plus one
assertion it adds, so the two share one namespace and an extension is not entitled to
renumber its base. A13 stays R6.3's and the wiring bound is A14. `instance-repository.md`

R6.3a is where the list is now declared to live, and it names its extensions. A15 is the third writing and its own: `specs/123-oss-install-experience/research.md` §4.4 argues for it — a scaffolded instance accepts an administrator created by its own CLI and answers that administrator's login with a session — and it takes the next free number for the same reason A14 did, an extension not being entitled to renumber its base.

A1.reason: The command's own `outwardReferences` derivation over the tree it wrote finds nothing naming anything above it. Evaluated before this run pins anything: publication's stand-in writes `file:` specifiers naming a directory outside the instance, and those are the harness's.

A2.reason: `pnpm install` succeeds outside the checkout, from packed tarballs, with no symlink back. The pinning is the closure of what the instance declares rather than the declaration itself — measured, a `pnpm install` fetches four module packages the manifest never names, as non-optional peers of packages it does, and an override does not reach an auto-installed peer.

A3.reason: 118 MIGRATIONS APPLIED, EXIT 0 — the first time a scaffolded instance has migrated a fresh database, and the milestone `specs/120-migration-closure-bridge-ownership/` was written to reach. The reason recorded here through T141 named the platform's own `Migration20260430T170044CoreSalesChannelsPromote` creating `sales_channel_cms_pages` with a foreign key to a table `cms` owns and the default module set does not ship, and counted seven more such reaches: that feature's Phase 2 moved all nine sales-channel bridges to the module owning each far side and Phase 3 moved the eight non-bridge references, two of them creations relocated between frozen bodies. THE LAST OPEN SITE WAS THIS FILE'S OWN SUBJECT AND PHASE 5 (FR-019) REMOVED IT: `Migration20260801T111001TransactionalEmailsEmailDefaultsReseed` `UPDATE`d `newsletter_email_blocks`, and the default module set is the `nonDeactivatable` closure, which does not include `newsletter` — so the two statements are gone from `up()` in place, with no rename and no replacement migration. The standing instrument is G4 in `backend/test/unit/db/instance-migration-order.test.ts`, which now reads zero: the next migration to name a table an instance cannot have fails there, in a unit run, rather than here after a twelve-minute scaffold.

A4.reason: GREEN, MEASURED ON THE MERGE OF `feat/121-platform-liveness` WITH A MASTER CARRYING `fix/instance-500-pipeline`, AND NEITHER BRANCH COULD HAVE TURNED IT GREEN ALONE. The run printed: "health 200 and the boot reconcile accounts for all 31 modules the presence route enumerates (installed=27 skipped=4)". A4 was two independent defects wearing one verdict, which is why it stood red while each was separately repaired. The first is D-229's: `/api/v1/_health` belonged to `health_checks`, a module declaring no `activation` block, so `endora new instance`'s `nonDeactivatable` closure never installed it and the route did not exist - feature 121 moves the route into the platform's own app builder and dissolves the module. The second is the request pipeline's: every other `/api/v1/*` path answered `500 INTERNAL` with nothing logged, because the boot-time `DefaultChannelReconciler` stood in `contributeReferenceDeployment` rather than in `composeApp`, an instance passes no `contribute` callback, and the kernel's global `onRequest` hook therefore threw `NoSystemDefaultChannel` on a `sales_channels` table with zero rows. `/api/v1/_health` was the single path `shouldResolve` excludes, which is why the two defects never showed the same symptom and were mistaken for one for a week. Recorded as the run printed it, on a scaffolded instance outside any checkout. The previous reason is kept below.
A4.previousReason: MEASURED ON `feat/121-platform-liveness`: THE HEALTH ROUTE ANSWERS 200 AND THIS ASSERTION IS NOW BLOCKED BY ITS SECOND HALF ALONE. The verdict moved `fail` -> `unmeasured` and the move is the whole of feature 121 (`specs/121-platform-liveness-probe/`, owner ruling D-229): the liveness probe is registered by `@endora-commerce/platform` itself — `composeApp` puts `healthRoutePlugin({ orm, redis })` at the head of the module plugins every root hands to `buildServer` — so a scaffolded instance serves `/api/v1/_health` because it is an Endora instance. The previous reason recorded here is kept below because it is the measurement that produced the ruling, and reading it is how the next reader knows what changed. What it described was a 404 from the instance's own `setNotFoundHandler`: the route belonged to the `health_checks` module, that module declared no `activation` block at all (D-36a item 4), no manifest declared it as a dependency, and `endora new instance` writes the closure over the modules declaring `nonDeactivatable` — so a default instance did not install it and the route did not exist. The module is dissolved; `evaluateA4` now passes its `healthStatus === 200` gate and its `reconcile !== null` gate, and stops at `enumerated === null`. WHAT IS LEFT IS THE SECOND A4 FINDING, WHICH IS NOT THIS FEATURE'S AND IS LARGER: `/api/v1/storefront/module-presence` does not answer, so there is no independent count to hold the reconcile line to and `installed > 0` is all a pass could mean. That is the same defect as *every other route on the booted instance answers 500 `INTERNAL` with nothing logged*, `/api/v1/openapi.json` among them — a route that touches no module and no database failing that way puts it in the request pipeline rather than in any container name. It is recorded in `specs/117-instance-bring-up/tasks.md`, it is reproduced and unrepaired, and no part of D-229 touches it. `unmeasured` rather than `fail` is therefore the honest state: the assertion's first half is green and its second has no subject to judge. THE 404 MEASUREMENT THAT PRODUCED D-229, KEPT VERBATIM: THE INSTANCE BOOTS AND LISTENS, AND THIS ASSERTION CANNOT GO GREEN FOR A REASON NOTHING IN THE WIRING CAN CHANGE. The reason recorded here through D-227 named `AwilixResolutionError: Could not resolve 'paymentAdapterRegistry'`, raised inside `defineModuleRoutes`' `await register(scoped)` — route registration under `avvio`, not the boot phase — from `orders`' `() => cradle().paymentAdapterRegistry` accessor. D-228 ruled that no new mechanism was needed: `degrades-without`'s own definition obliges the declaring module to check presence before it reads, and `isPresent` collapses never-installed and switched-off into `false`, so one probe answers both axes. `specs/117-instance-bring-up/` Phase 6 gave the three `orders` accessors that probe and the `| null` beside it, and passed the accessor whole into `OrderService` rather than invoking it while routes were being registered — which also closes the captured-registration fail-open D-228 measured underneath. MEASURED on the repaired tree, three times through this criterion and once by booting the kept instance directly: 118 migrations, `module:install --all` reports 30 installed, every boot hook runs to completion, and the process reports `Server listening at http://127.0.0.1:3555`. The health route then answers **404, not 200** — which is this instance's own `setNotFoundHandler`, so the failure is no longer a process that died. WHAT STANDS BETWEEN THIS 404 AND A VERDICT IS NOT A WIRING DEFECT. `/api/v1/_health` is `health_checks`' route; that module declares no `activation` block at all (D-36a item 4), no module declares it as a dependency, and `endora new instance` writes the `nonDeactivatable` closure — so a default instance does not install it and the route does not exist. This assertion is therefore unreachable as written, and the question is the owner's: does the default module set include `health_checks`, does the liveness route become the platform's, or does the criterion probe something a default instance serves? A SECOND RED IS REPRODUCED AND NOT YET OWNED: every other route on the booted instance answers 500 `INTERNAL` with nothing logged, `/api/v1/openapi.json` and `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login` among them. A route that touches no module and no database failing that way puts the defect in the request pipeline rather than in any container name, and it is outside Phase 6's subject: it is reachable by neither a module registration nor a `composeApp` value, and it could not have been observed before, because until D-228's repair no scaffolded instance had ever reached the point of serving a request. THE ELEVEN CONTAINER NAMES `backend/src/composition.ts` supplied and `composeApp` did not are drained by the same feature (FR-033) and moved this assertion not at all, which is the honest record rather than a shortfall: they are read per request, so a supply gap in them has no boot-time verdict to move. `check:port-dependencies` now refuses the class outright — `instance-unsupplied`, at zero (FR-034).

A5.reason: The built admin bundle names exactly the installed module packages that publish an admin layer — 23 of 30 installed, over 3.6 MiB of JavaScript, measured on the bundle and not on the registry that produced it. The expectation is read off each installed package's own `exports` map and the evidence off the bundle, which is two authors on purpose, as `evaluateA3` already recomputes the migration order rather than reading the one the platform logged. T138 wrote the member; what it also needed was `endora generate`, because the renderer of `contracts/instance-tree.md` §2.6's two artefacts lived in `backend/scripts` and no client can reach it.

A6.reason: GREEN, AND IT LANDED RED. Measured: the built site serves 72 pages and its navigation names a routed page for exactly the 27 of 30 installed module packages that ship a `docs/` layer, both directions. The navigation half was clean from the first measurement — T137 wrote the documentation member (`contracts/instance-tree.md` §2.4a) and moved the renderers into `@endora-commerce/cli` — and what was red was the **build**, under `onBrokenLinks: 'throw'`, over four broken links of two kinds. Three were a module page linking this repository's own site tree (`../architecture/custom-fields.md`, `../integrations/api-access.md`): refused by nothing in the estate, and broken in **every** instance whatever its module set, because a page above the modules category is the site's own content and travels with no package. 8 such links stood in 6 module packages. They are repaired and locked at zero by `check:module-docs`' `site-tree-link`, which carries no ledger because there is no instance in which such a link resolves (`specs/conventions/check-inventory.md`; `specs/conventions/module-documentation.md` item 1b). The fourth was the other kind — `catalog`'s `attributes.md` -> `../search.md`, a sibling the default set does not install — and it drained with them: `backend/scripts/ledgers/foreign-module-links/catalog.ts` keeps `promotions`, which that set does install. WHAT KEEPS IT GREEN IS NOT THIS RECORD. `site-tree-link` refuses the first kind outright, and `foreign-module-link`'s two-way shards refuse an unledgered one of the second — but a *ledgered* sibling link in a module the default set installs would pass every check in the estate and red this assertion, which is the case `specs/100-module-owned-documentation/`'s Phase 2 drain exists for and the reason A6 is worth running rather than inferring.

A7.reason: MEASURED, ALL THREE HALVES, AS THE RUN PRINTED IT: "none of the 42 module packages this instance did not install is named in the built admin bundle, owns any of the 463 endpoints it serves — measured against the 475 route identities their published `./backend` layers own — or appears among the 31 modules it enumerates, every one of which is one of the 30 it installed or is entitled to be there without being an installed package (_lifecycle)". T142 is the row, and A4 passing that morning is what gave two of the three halves a subject. THE API-SURFACE HALF IS WORTH READING TWICE, because the obvious instrument for it is wrong. Matching an absent module's **name** against the served path segments reports `organizations`' `/restrictions/payment-methods` and `promotions`' `/rule-targets/payment-methods` as the uninstalled `payment_methods` module advertising itself — measured, two hits, both of them English rather than a defect. So the expectation is derived from each absent package's own published `./backend` instead: 475 route identities, through the same `instanceComposition` derivation `endora generate` uses, against the OpenAPI document the running instance serves. Two authors, which is `evaluateA5`'s arrangement one surface over. A parameterised endpoint is one identity in both spellings — `{id}` out of the document, `:id` off the registration — and is normalised before the comparison; comparing them literally would report every one of them clean. THE ENUMERATION HALF ALSO ASKS THE COMPLETENESS QUESTION, and it is not the same one: an enumerated id that is in no packed catalogue at all passes the first form and is still a module the client did not install. The one id here that is not an installed package is `_lifecycle`, which the **installed platform package** ships and this run reads out of that package (`@endora-commerce/platform/lifecycle`'s own `manifest.id`) rather than out of a list. THE NOTE THE RUN PRINTS BESIDE IT IS NOT ABSORBED BY THIS PASS: the install pulls in 8 `@endora-commerce` packages the instance's manifest never names, four of them module packages, and the platform's runtime discovery composes such a package exactly as a declared one. They are **installed**, so they are not this assertion's subject — A7 asks what the instance did not install, not what it did not declare — and the distance between the declared set and the composed set is a finding of its own, standing in that note and belonging to FR-022 rather than here.

A8.reason: RED, AND THE RED IS THE FINDING. As the run printed it: "'instance_acceptance_overlay' is composed and its wrap of 'instanceAcceptanceOverlayService' is live in the container, and the rendered report carries no `decoration` entry for it — 1 entries: registration:instance_acceptance_overlay:instanceAcceptanceOverlayService; findings: [stale-reason] apps/instance/divergence.ts: `decoration:instance_acceptance_overlay:instanceAcceptanceOverlayService` describes no divergence in this tree | [unowned-subject] apps/instance/modules/instance_acceptance_overlay/backend.ts:22: 'instanceAcceptanceOverlayService' is registered by no module in the composition". THE COMPOSED HALF IS GREEN and is a first: the criterion writes an overlay module into `apps/<deployment>/modules/`, supplies `DEPLOYMENT`, installs it and boots — the module's own route answers 200 and the value behind its own registration carries the wrap's marker, so a deployment's overlay module reaches a running instance. WHAT IS RED IS THE REPORT, AND THE DERIVATION IT COMES FROM CONTRADICTS ITSELF IN ONE FILE: the same rendering carries `registration:instance_acceptance_overlay:instanceAcceptanceOverlayService` — it knows the overlay module registers that name — and then reports a decoration of it as `unowned-subject`, whose own remedy text says *"registered by no module in the composition. Composition throws for it at boot"*, which is measurably untrue of a tree that booted. The owner map `instanceComposition` builds has two sources, the installed packages and the platform's root-supplied names, and the deployment's own overlay registrations are in neither. THE DECORATED NAME IS NOT A CHOICE THIS CRITERION HAD, and all three candidates are measured. (a) An installed package's registration: refused at composition by `PackageDecorationNotOfferedError` (D-176 Q3, and in an instance **every** module is an installed package) — measured on `price_lists`' `pricingService`, and the report would have recorded it cleanly. (b) A root-supplied name, which D-156.4 sanctions in so many words: every one of them is registered `asValue`, awilix marks such a resolver `isLeakSafe` and carries no lifetime, and `ctx.di.decorate` re-registers the wrapper as `asFunction(...).setLifetime(inner.lifetime ?? Lifetime.TRANSIENT)` — so the wrap leaks both, and the first singleton that resolves the name kills the boot with `AwilixResolutionError: ... has a shorter lifetime than its ancestor`. Measured twice: `commandBus` behind `catalog`, `storefrontBaseUrl` behind `organizations`. (c) The overlay module's own registration — the only one a booting instance accepts, and the one the fixture uses. So the intersection of *what an instance will compose* and *what the report will attribute* is empty today, and this entry is that measurement rather than a bad fixture. IT IS `fail` AND NOT `unmeasured` DELIBERATELY: both halves ran, one answered and one did not, which is a verdict. It retires when the instance host's owner map takes the deployment's own overlay registrations — the derivation already lists them as `registration` sites in the same run — or when a package may declare a registration decoratable, which is the exit `PackageDecorationNotOfferedError`'s own message names. Both belong to `specs/107-override-report-and-ladder/` and to this feature's T138a, not to T141/T142, and neither is repaired here: the merge request that measures a thing is not the place to also repair it.

A9.reason: MEASURED, AS THE RUN PRINTED IT: "a read of OrganizationInvitation (organization_invitations) with no tenant context is refused by `MissingTenantContextError`, the same read widened returns rows of 2 organizations — so it is a read that would have crossed a tenant boundary — and pinned to one it returns that one's rows alone". `contracts/instance-repository.md` R6.3 is the assertion and T141 is the row. IT IS A PROCESS OF ITS OWN INSIDE THE INSTANCE (`backend/scripts/acceptance/instance-tenancy-probe.ts`), resolving the instance's packages through a `createRequire` rooted at its **backend member** and running with its `cwd` there: rooted at the workspace root it resolved a `@mikro-orm/postgresql` of a different patch from the `@mikro-orm/migrations` the member's own ORM configuration loads, and with our `cwd` MikroORM's version check read this repository's copy beside the instance's and refused the pair. NOTHING IN IT NAMES AN ENTITY: the subject is chosen from the instance's own ORM metadata — the entities carrying the `org` global filter, smallest required-property set first, and the first one the probe can actually write a row of per tenant. Six were tried and refused by their own foreign keys before `OrganizationInvitation` took one, and the report says which answered. THE SECOND LEG IS WHAT STOPS THE FIRST BEING VACUOUS. A guard that refuses a read of an empty table has refused nothing, so the identical query is run under `withSystemScope` and comes back holding two organizations' rows: the query the guard refused is therefore demonstrably one that would have crossed a tenant boundary. Fewer than two organizations in it is recorded as `unmeasured` by `evaluateA9` and never as a pass. ONE HALF IS NARROWER THAN THE REQUEST PIPELINE'S AND THE REASON IS THE PUBLISHED SURFACE. A `single-org` context is derived server-side from an authenticated actor; of the four modes an instance's own packages let a process establish exactly two, none and `withSystemScope`. `withOrgScope` exists in the platform's `tenancy/escape-hatch.ts` and `./tenancy` does not export it, and reaching past the exports map for it would make this verdict depend on an internal path that can move. So the narrowing is measured through the published derived-scope helper `orgConstraintFor`, which is the constraint a module applies where the column filter cannot reach, and the ambient-filter form of that leg waits on either a published context runner or an authenticated request — a bound API key resolves `single-org` (feature 062) and is the route a later step would take.

A10.reason: A module set missing a required module is refused with exit 1, the target directory untouched, and the refusal carries verbatim the `activation.reason` an installed manifest declares — which is what R5.6 and D-100 ask for and what an exit-code check alone would not see. The sentences are read out of the packages this run resolved, never from a list in the criterion.

A11.reason: Both halves have a subject now: `@endora-commerce/platform` and `@endora-commerce/admin-shell` both resolve in the created instance, and none of the 27 files the command wrote is byte-identical to any of the 1036 those two packages ship. The counts are printed by the run rather than recorded here. Two things had to change for the second half to stop being vacuous: T138 wrote the admin member that depends on the shell, and the criterion learned to look for a package in a **member's** `node_modules` as well as the root's — pnpm installs a package where it is declared, so reading the root alone reported `admin-shell does not resolve` over a tree that had it.

A12.reason: It needs a fixture registry to publish a platform patch into and a second install to pick it up. T144, gated on F10 (`specs/071-modular-packaging/roadmap.md`).

A13.reason: 174 KiB of built stylesheet carries, for each of 16 packages — the shell and 15 module admin layers — a class only that package uses, so its presence can only be explained by that package's own sources having been scanned. A5 says the screens are in the bundle; this says they are visible. Three exclusions keep the witness honest and each was measured rather than reasoned: a token is read only out of a `class`/`className` position (every string literal made i18n keys and DOM ids look like classes and reported seven modules as unscanned), a class the design system's own imported `theme.css` defines is evidence of nothing in either direction, and a token carrying a `.` is escaped in the compiled CSS and could never be matched. A package with no class of its own is counted and skipped, never failed.

A14.reason: 248 lines of wiring across the 13 files the command classified as wiring, counted on disk in the created tree rather than on the plan, against R1.4's bound of 250. RE-MEASURED, NEVER ADJUSTED BY A DELTA. It was 242 over 12 files until `specs/123-oss-install-experience/` G2 added the thirteenth — `backend/src/cli.ts`, six lines, the operator CLI whose absence meant a scaffolded instance could run no command at all. Six of the eight lines of headroom that record named are now spent and **two are left**, which is the number to check before adding a fourteenth: the dispatch that file calls is 479 lines and lives in `@endora-commerce/platform/cli`, so what a client's tree pays for the whole operator CLI is one `runCli({ deploymentRoot })`. `specs/122-layer-deployment-independence/` Phase 2's `deploy/` examples moved this not at all: they are the **client's** kind, which is the classification doing its job rather than a coincidence. IT WAS 241 BEFORE T137 and that line is `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s third member: §2.4a's four files are all `client` or `derived`, so the documentation member adds no wiring of its own.

A15.reason: GREEN, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME ANYBODY HAS SIGNED IN TO A SCAFFOLDED INSTANCE. Recorded verbatim from the run of 2026-09-13 that added it: `A15 PASS — the instance own CLI created an administrator and POST /api/v1/auth/admin/login answered 200 with the admin session cookie set`. IT TOOK TWO MERGES AND NEITHER WOULD HAVE BEEN ENOUGH ALONE. `specs/123-oss-install-experience/` G2 supplied the first half: `endora new instance` reported `backend/src/cli.ts` as an omission, so a scaffolded instance ran no command its modules declared, had no `admin:create`, and the admin bundle A5 and A13 prove is built and styled had nobody to log in as. G2 moved `backend/src/cli/demo-command.ts` into `@endora-commerce/platform/demo` — where `test/unit/kernel/host-residue-partition.test.ts` had it ledgered as platform-shaped residue with a `retiredBy` naming exactly that move — and the dispatch around it into `@endora-commerce/platform/cli`, so the entry point the scaffolder renders is five lines and holds a copy of none of it (D-207). No subpath was added: both are host-internal under D-160.14 and `check:platform-surface` is green with no ledger key moved. THE SECOND HALF IS `fix/instance-500-pipeline`, MERGED THE SAME DAY. On the run that added this assertion the login answered `500 INTERNAL` — the request-pipeline defect A4 records — and it was recorded here as a `fail` naming that. `composeApp` now runs `DefaultChannelReconciler` itself, so the `NoSystemDefaultChannel` every `/api/v1/*` request was raising in the sales-channel `onRequest` hook is gone; measured again on the rebased tree, the same login answers 200 with `b2b_admin_session` set. Both halves are load-bearing and this assertion is the only thing that measures their conjunction. ONE PREMISE FAILED TO RE-DERIVE AND IS CORRECTED HERE. `specs/123-oss-install-experience/research.md` §4.3 and §4.4 name the route `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login`, and so does A4's own reason above. Nothing registers that path. `admin_users`' `src/backend/routes.public.ts` declares `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/login`, which is what this assertion probes; a probe of the documented spelling would have measured a 404 for ever while reporting on the login. RE-MEASURED ONCE MORE AFTER FEATURE 121 MERGED, and the criterion then had no red at all: `pass=11 fail=0 unmeasured=4 of 15`, A4 at `health 200 and the boot reconcile accounts for all 31 modules the presence route enumerates`. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: a 200 with no `Set-Cookie` is a **fail** here, not a pass, because `mfaRequired` and `mfaSetupRequired` are both 200 and neither is a session.
